name: kinetic-text
title: Kinetic Text
description: Three stacked lines of text whose individual letters thicken as the pointer passes over them, with the neighbours taking a smaller boost. It reads like type reacting to touch.
use: A headline should invite the pointer and show off typography without colour or motion.
avoid: Body copy or menus, where shifting weights hurt reading and the padding makes words jitter.
a11y: Each letter is hidden from assistive tech with a readable copy supplied, but the effect is hover-only and ignores reduced motion. (keyboard: n-a, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: Three centred lines of white sans-serif text on black, in descending sizes: a large heading, a medium line and a small line. Most letters are light-weight, and a short run near the pointer turns noticeably heavier, giving the line an uneven ripple of thickness.
behaves: As the pointer crosses a line the letter under it thickens to a heavy weight and gains a faint outline and extra side padding, while the glyphs either side thicken slightly less. All of it eases back to light within half a second of leaving.
customise: The words come from a text prop and the wrapper element from as; size and colour come from className, while weights and the neighbour response are fixed in the classes.
weight: light: One span per letter with CSS weight, stroke and padding transitions, no script.
demo: Lines reading "Hover over me!", "Kinetic Typography" and "Each letter reacts independently"
issues: Letters take side padding as they thicken, so words jitter sideways while the pointer moves.
polishWhy: Light, characterful type response; the padding-driven sideways jitter is the only wobble.
